newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma to curb Suu Kyi movement until protests end.
newsitem.headline: Burma to curb Suu Kyi movement until protests end.

text.p: Restrictions on Burmese opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi's movements will remain for as long as student unrest continues, a military government spokesman said on Thursday.
When asked how long the restrictions would be in force, the spokesman told Reuters: "As long as the situation still does not go back to normal."
He said the Nobel laureate and leader of the National League for Democracy (NLD) party had been asked to temporarily stay at home for her own safety.

Thousands of students last week launched street protests to demand more political freedom. The ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) detained more than 860 of the protestors but later freed them.
The military government has since tightened security in Rangoon, closed universities and broken the momentum of the students, preventing them from taking to the streets.
The students and the NLD have denied any link with each other. But the goverment said some NLD members, communist elements and student exiles were inciting the students.

Aides to Suu Kyi, who has remained in her lakeside Rangoon residence to avoid being drawn into the student protest, said she had requested government permission to leave her home on Tuesday to see a senior U.S. Embassy official.
The request was turned down, the aides said. They declined to say what Suu Kyi had planned to discuss with the embassy official.
The government spokesman confirmed that the request had been turned down.
"We know what they're up to. We thought it was not a very good time for her to go out," he added.

"As you know, we've made it convenient for her and her NLD members to hold meetings in her compound... but until this fluid situation (is over), it's very easy to create problems when she's outside," he said.
The spokesman had accused the U.S. Embassy on Wednesday of trying to use the restrictions on Suu Kyi's movements as an excuse for imposing sanctions against Burma.
He had alleged that the U.S. embassy urged her to ask for permission to leave home, knowing that it would be refused.
A U.S. embassy official denied the assertion.
